comparison_against_frozen_baselines.reading: context at first Rust write is below the corrected pre-change median while pre-write read calls are ABOVE it. Under the registered disambiguation rule that pattern is earlier committing, not leaner reading. n=1.
comparison_against_frozen_baselines.confound_that_blocks_any_causal_reading: P1's named read set is 1,064 lines against B1 builders reading a ~2,700-line Rust crate plus contract sections. A smaller read set lowers this metric for a reason the treatment does not claim. This is exactly the confound prereg amendment 2 named when it restated the criterion.

whether the 150,000 trigger fires for a single-slice port, and the handoff turnaround if it does
first in-repo JS->Rust expansion ratio (added Rust lines per JS line), which R1 could not give because R1 was greenfield
Mwt per 1k added Rust lines for a port, as a new comparator with no prior baseline

H2: n=1 cannot distinguish 0 of 1 from the 14.3% base rate

gating_cost_before_any_code.note: scout + alignment = 1.707 Mwt spent establishing that R2 does not apply here and that the design still wants this component. Both were read-only and both changed the plan.

root_context.observation: the successor root crossed the 150,000 trigger 73 minutes after the transfer that reset it to 51,954. Relevant to R3 and to the root-transfer economics: a root reaches the trigger quickly, which is consistent with the measured 1.4-call break-even rather than against it.

instrument_note: No live poller was run for this cohort. R1 defect R1-M-002 came from a watcher that derived idleness from transcript mtime; a single-builder cohort is fully recoverable post hoc from the transcript, so the instrument was omitted rather than repeated.
